benchmark_name: Evaluating the Quality of Psychotherapy Conversational Agents: Framework Development and Cross-Sectional Study
institutions: Department of Psychiatry and Biobehavioral Sciences, University of California, Los Angeles; Department of Psychology, College of Arts and Science, University of San Francisco
ground_truth_source: CAPE framework criteria (34 items across 8 sections) scored by 2 human raters using fictional personas to simulate psychotherapy interactions; items scored yes/no (0 or 1), averaged into subscores per section
size_of_benchmark: 34 items across 8 sections (CAPE framework); 4 chatbots × 2 personas × 2 raters = 16 conversations evaluated
what_assessed_skills: Background/transparency; therapeutic orientation; therapeutic alliance and boundaries; conversational capabilities; monitoring and risk evaluation; privacy and harm; accessibility; training data and knowledge base transparency
tasks_assessed: Simulated psychotherapy conversation (multi-turn); rapport-building; crisis/suicidality detection and escalation; psychoeducation and coping skill delivery; personalized response generation; privacy policy transparency; accessibility evaluation
population_represented: General public users of psychotherapy chatbots; represented via 2 fictional personas: male with MDD (no specifiers) and female with MDD with peripartum onset
evaluation_method: Human evaluation by 2 raters applying the CAPE framework to chatbot transcripts generated via persona-based role-play interactions. Metrics: section subscores (0–1 scale, averaged from binary item scores); interrater reliability via Cohen's κ (0.81–0.87 within-conversation; 0.69–0.82 cross-conversation); pairwise differences tested via t-tests and Wilcoxon signed rank tests. Evaluation: Human.
llms_evaluated: Therapist • Psychologist CBT Therapy (nonmedical therapy) [custom GPT-4o]; Psychology Psychologist (nonmedical) [custom GPT-4o]; Therapist • Psychologist CBT Therapy (nonmedical) [custom GPT-4o]; Precision Psychology [custom GPT-4o] — all based on OpenAI GPT-4o
mental_health_conditions: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD); MDD with peripartum onset; suicidality (crisis scenarios); general depression and mental health support
performance_scores: Background subscores: 0.83–1; Therapeutic approach subscores: 0 (all chatbots); Therapeutic alliance & boundaries: 0.75–1; Conversational capabilities: 0.83–1; Monitoring & risk evaluation: 0.67–0.75; Privacy & harm: 0.83–1 (Precision Psychology significantly lower: mean 0.017, SD 0.00; t3=∞; P<.001); Accessibility: 0.80–0.95; Training data/knowledge base: 0 (all chatbots)
short_summary: This paper introduces the CAPE (Conversational Agent for Psychotherapy Evaluation) framework, a modular 34-item tool with 8 sections for assessing the quality of LLM-based psychotherapy chatbots. The authors evaluated 4 popular custom GPT-4o chatbots from OpenAI's GPT Store using a persona-based role-play approach with 2 fictional clients representing major depressive disorder. Two human raters independently scored each chatbot across CAPE sections using multi-turn conversations. Chatbots performed well on rapport-building, conversational capabilities, and accessibility, but uniformly failed on therapeutic orientation adherence and training data transparency, and showed weaknesses in monitoring/risk evaluation. The Precision Psychology chatbot scored significantly lower on privacy due to personalized advertising behavior.
